pr_title: Guard against os.get_blocking not being available
pr_comments: The CI error appears to be unrelated to my change, can we get it re-checked?

Heh, well, ignoring the fact that running Ansible on Windows natively via Cygwin/msys/whatever is unsupported (and playing with fire, trust me- it *will* break)... It wasn't our intent to have a hard exit for OS's that can't tell us about this- the underlying issue we were fixing is unlikely to be a problem for Windows.

I'd be OK merging something like this if it was a little more defensive and just a warning- there's a lot of other places that could chuck `AttributeError` in your proposed change. eg, just add a `hasattr` check for `get_blocking` and do a `warnings.warn` with `RuntimeWarning` about an unsupported OS if it's not there (since it's so early, we don't have `Display` available yet).

> Heh, well, ignoring the fact that running Ansible on Windows natively via Cygwin/msys/whatever is unsupported (and playing with fire, trust me- it _will_ break)... It wasn't our intent to have a hard exit for OS's that can't tell us about this

My reading of the [code](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/77668/files#diff-8b63e98657502798586c7e73798fe175c91045d968af3cc41839f07cfcd9fde1R36) was that it was indeed made to have it hard exit for OS's that don't have blocking IO.

I was not part of the review process for that change, so I can't divine what the author's intent was beyond just reading the code that was present and making an assumption that this was the desired behavior. I agree that Windows/cygwin/etc is going to blow up in weird and difficult ways, so my intent was to have it exit with a legible error instead of exploding with a stack trace, since that appears to be the behavior that is desired when `handles` evaluates to a `True`

As for @webknjaz 's review suggestions, my change was to make this change as _minimal_ as possible since frankly I am not a frequent contributor to Ansible and was not looking to make a large change in this part where I don't have a lot of context as to the whys/hows.

@mattclay do you mind if I ask you for an opinion?
I still believe that catching the exception and printing a useful error message and exiting is better than just crashing with a stack trace
I don't have time to work on this, closing.

issue_context.title: OS.get_blocking is not present on all platforms
issue_context.body:
### Summary

#77668 changed Ansible so that it requires blocking IO. That's fine, however the logic is not correct. The `os` module for platforms that do not have blocking IO do not have that function available.

For example, on windows:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\Sean\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python310\lib\runpy.py", line 196, in _run_module_as_main
    return _run_code(code, main_globals, None,
  File "C:\Users\Sean\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python310\lib\runpy.py", line 86, in _run_code
    exec(code, run_globals)
  File "C:\Users\Sean\src\vagrant-containerlab\.venv\Scripts\ansible-playbook.exe\__main__.py", line 4, in <module>
  File "C:\Users\Sean\src\vagrant-containerlab\.venv\lib\site-packages\ansible\cli\__init__.py", line 42, in <module>
    check_blocking_io()
  File "C:\Users\Sean\src\vagrant-containerlab\.venv\lib\site-packages\ansible\cli\__init__.py", line 34, in check_blocking_io
    if not os.get_blocking(fd):
AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'get_blocking'
```

The logic should handle this `AttributeError` and exit with the correct error message that Ansible requires blocking IO, instead of crashing.

### Issue Type

Bug Report

### Component Name

cli

### Ansible Version

```console
$ ansible --version

Cannot get version because crashes early
```


### Configuration

```console
Cannot get configuration because crashes early
```


### OS / Environment

Windows

### Steps to Reproduce

`anisble-playbook`

### Expected Results

Should exit with legible error

### Actual Results

```console
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\Sean\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python310\lib\runpy.py", line 196, in _run_module_as_main
    return _run_code(code, main_globals, None,
  File "C:\Users\Sean\AppData\Local\Programs\Python\Python310\lib\runpy.py", line 86, in _run_code
    exec(code, run_globals)
  File "C:\Users\Sean\src\vagrant-containerlab\.venv\Scripts\ansible.exe\__main__.py", line 4, in <module>
  File "C:\Users\Sean\src\vagrant-containerlab\.venv\lib\site-packages\ansible\cli\__init__.py", line 42, in <module>
    check_blocking_io()
  File "C:\Users\Sean\src\vagrant-containerlab\.venv\lib\site-packages\ansible\cli\__init__.py", line 34, in check_blocking_io
    if not os.get_blocking(fd):
AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'get_blocking'
```

review_comments:
OTOH, Matt is right — we don't care enough about this to sabotage the entire process at this point, I think:
```suggestion
        try:
            fd_blocking_io_enabled = os.get_blocking(fd)
        except AttributeError:
            print(
                'ERROR: Ansible requires blocking IO, but this platform '
                'does not have os.get_blocking available',
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            fd_blocking_io_enabled = False

        if not fd_blocking_io_enabled:
            handles.append(getattr(handle, 'name', None) or '#%s' % fd)
```

Actually, looking closer, a `os_exposes_get_blocking = hasattr(os, 'get_blocking')` could be performed at the very beginning of the function and used as a guard expression to exit the function early, not even going into the loop. So I'd leave the loop contents alone.
